summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM concealing base64 JS that fetches and executes remote Python payload
details: The package advertises itself as a TLS self-signed certificate helper, but test/key.pem is not an RSA key: the body between the PEM markers base64-decodes to a JavaScript snippet. index.js reads test/key.pem on every generateCertificates() call, strips the PEM markers, base64-decodes the body, and passes the decoded string as a third argument to selfsign.generate() (from the pinned self-sign@^5.6.3 dependency), which evaluates it. The decoded JavaScript contains a second-layer base64 constant that decodes to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches that URL, and pipes the response body into a detached `python3 -` (or `python` on win32) child process spawned with windowsHide and all stdio suppressed, executing attacker-controlled Python with the caller's privileges. The domain aptupdate.org is unrelated to certificate generation, and the double-base64-inside-a-fake-PEM layering is evasion of automated scanning and human review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
